mainTopic: מרדכי as בלשן, the public עומר harvest ceremony, and the ניסן celebration days marking victories over the צדוקים and בייתוסים
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of מרדכי. A משנה calls him פתחיה because he 'opened up' hard topics and knew seventy languages. The גמרא objects that every judge of the סנהדרין knew seventy languages. It answers that מרדכי could mix languages together and interpret them, which is why he is called בלשן. Then a new משנה describes the עומר harvest. Court messengers tie the barley in advance, crowds gather, and at nightfall the messenger asks about the sunset, the sickle, the basket and שבת, three times each. The משנה explains that all this publicity was aimed against the בייתוסים, who denied reaping the עומר on the night after the first day of פסח. The גמרא brings a ברייתא about celebration days in ניסן, marking the victories over the צדוקים on the תמיד and over the בייתוסים on the date of שבועות. The amud ends with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rejecting an old בייתוסי's weak reason with a פסוק, and the point of that פסוק is explained on the next amud.

steps.title: מרדכי is called פתחיה because he knew seventy languages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the earlier story about מרדכי's skill with a משנה that identifies פתחיה as מרדכי and explains his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what we learned in a משנה: פתחיה, who was in charge of the bird offerings, is מרדכי. Why was he called פתחיה? Because he would 'open up' hard topics and explain them, and he knew seventy languages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up what it just said about מרדכי's skill with words and languages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name פתחיה is read as coming from 'פתח', to open. He opened up difficult matters and explained them. The משנה also says he knew seventy languages, which fits the story the גמרא just told about him.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of bird offerings (doves or pigeons)
The name given to מרדכי, related to 'opening' matters
Seventy languages, meaning all the languages of the nations
He interprets them and explains them

phrases.english: And this is what we learned in a משנה:
Petachya was in charge of the bird offerings
this is Mordechai;
why was he called Petachya?
Because he would open up matters and explain them,
and he knew seventy languages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier story about מרדכי's language skill with a משנה
steps.raayaObject: That מרדכי was famous for his mastery of languages and interpretation
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שקלים that identifies פתחיה as מרדכי

steps.title: But every member of the סנהדרין knew seventy languages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: knowing seventy languages is nothing special, since it was a requirement for every member of the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the members of the סנהדרין also knew seventy languages! As רבי יוחנן said: they seat on the סנהדרין only people of wisdom, good appearance, height, and age, who know about sorcery and know seventy languages, so that the סנהדרין will not have to hear testimony through a translator.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה praises מרדכי for knowing seventy languages, if every judge on the סנהדרין had to know them anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן lists the requirements for sitting on the סנהדרין, and seventy languages is one of them. So that skill cannot be what made מרדכי stand out. The משנה must mean something more.

keyTerms.meaning: The great court of 71 judges
Experts in sorcery, people who understand how it works
A translator or interpreter
People of good appearance

steps.confusionAlert: The judges were not sorcerers. They had to understand sorcery so they could judge people accused of it.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין נָמֵי יָדְעִי שִׁבְעִים לָשׁוֹן!
phrases.english: All the members of the Sanhedrin also knew seventy languages!
As Rabbi Yochanan said:
They seat on the Sanhedrin only
men of wisdom, men of good appearance,
men of height, men of mature age,
masters of sorcery,
and who know seventy languages,
so that the Sanhedrin will not have to hear testimony
from the mouth of a translator.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלְּהוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין נָמֵי יָדְעִי שִׁבְעִים לָשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's praise of מרדכי for knowing seventy languages
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that מרדכי was special because he knew seventy languages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every member of the סנהדרין had to know seventy languages, so this cannot be a special distinction

steps.title: מרדכי could mix languages together and interpret them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מרדכי's special skill was combining languages and drawing explanations from them, which is why he is called בלשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he could mix languages together and interpret them. That is why the פסוק calls מרדכי 'בלשן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: מרדכי did more than know languages. He could blend them together and draw meaning out of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every judge knew the seventy languages separately. מרדכי could take words from different languages, combine them, and explain them. The name בלשן is read as 'בלל' (mix) plus 'לשון' (language).

keyTerms.meaning: He mixed languages together
A name of מרדכי, read as 'one who mixes languages'
Rather, introducing a new answer

steps.whatToRemember: Knowing seventy languages was standard for the סנהדרין. מרדכי's unique gift was mixing languages and interpreting them, hinted in his name בלשן.

phrases.english: Rather, he would mix languages together and interpret them,
and this is what is written about Mordechai: “Bilshan.”
phrases.notes: נחמיה 7:7. The name is read as בלל (mix) plus לשון (language).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by redefining what was special about מרדכי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the praise: it was not knowing languages but combining them
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה praised מרדכי only for knowing seventy languages, which every judge knew
steps.terutzMaskana: מרדכי could mix languages and interpret them, as shown by his name בלשן

steps.title: How the עומר barley was prepared and harvested
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes how the court's messengers prepared the barley for the עומר and how the nearby towns gathered for the harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How did they do it? Messengers of the בית דין went out on ערב יום טוב and tied the barley into bundles while it was still attached to the ground, so it would be easy to cut. All the towns near that place gathered there, so the harvest would be done with great fanfare.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the steps of preparing and harvesting the barley for the עומר offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two practical details are given. First, messengers tied the stalks into bundles ahead of time, while still growing, so the cutting would be quick. Second, people from nearby towns came to make the harvest a large public event.

keyTerms.meaning: Messengers sent by the court
The day before the festival (here, פסח)
Bundles or sheaves
Still attached to the ground
Great fanfare, a large public event

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the description of the עומר harvest. The גמרא will go on to discuss these details.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How would they do it?
phrases.notes: He means: how did they carry out the harvest of the עומר?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלוּחֵי בֵּית דִּין יוֹצְאִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: Messengers of the court would go out on the eve of the festival,
and they would make them into bundles
while still attached to the ground,
so that it would be easy to reap.
All the towns near that place
would gather there,
so that it would be harvested with great fanfare.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה about the procedure of the עומר harvest
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Court messengers tie the barley into bundles on ערב פסח while it is still attached, and nearby towns gather so the harvest is done with great fanfare

steps.title: At nightfall the messenger asks the crowd questions
steps.stepSummary: Once it gets dark, the court's messenger asks the crowd whether the sun has set and whether to use this sickle and this basket. The crowd answers 'yes' each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it got dark, the messenger asked the people: 'Did the sun set?' They said: 'Yes.' Again: 'Did the sun set?' 'Yes.' 'This sickle?' 'Yes.' 'This sickle?' 'Yes.' 'This basket?' 'Yes.' 'This basket?' 'Yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its description of the עומר harvest. It shows the back-and-forth between the messenger and the crowd right before reaping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail gets public approval before anything is cut: that the time has come (sunset), the tool (the sickle), and the container (the basket). Turning every step into a loud public exchange makes the event impossible to miss. Step 9 explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: It grew dark (nightfall).
Yes.
Sickle, the curved blade used for cutting grain.
Basket, used here to hold the cut barley.

phrases.english: Once it grew dark, he says to them:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the messenger of the בית דין from the previous step. 'Them' is the crowd that gathered from nearby towns.

phrases.english: "Did the sun set?" They say: "Yes."
"Did the sun set?" They say: "Yes."
"With this sickle?" They say: "Yes."
"With this sickle?" They say: "Yes."
"Into this basket?" They say: "Yes."
"Into this basket?" They say: "Yes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 4, moving from the preparations to the moment of reaping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before reaping the עומר, the messenger publicly confirms sunset, the sickle and the basket, and the crowd answers 'yes' each time.

steps.title: Extra questions when the reaping falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: If the reaping falls on שבת, the messenger also asks 'This שבת?' and 'Shall I reap?', and the crowd answers 'yes' and 'reap'.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת he asked them: 'This שבת?' They said: 'Yes.' Again: 'This שבת?' 'Yes.' 'Shall I reap?' They answered: 'Reap.' Again: 'Shall I reap?' 'Reap.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds what happens when the reaping falls on שבת. The crowd openly approves reaping even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally reaping is forbidden on שבת. Here the crowd loudly confirms that it is שבת and still says 'reap'. This shows that the עומר harvest happens at its set time even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This שבת?', asking the crowd to confirm the day is שבת.
'Shall I reap?'
'Reap!', the crowd's command to go ahead.

phrases.english: On Shabbat, he says to them:
"On this Shabbat?" They say: "Yes."
"On this Shabbat?" They say: "Yes."
"Shall I reap?" And they say to him: "Reap."
"Shall I reap?" And they say to him: "Reap."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the special questions asked when the reaping falls on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the reaping falls on שבת, the crowd publicly confirms it is שבת and still tells the messenger to reap.

steps.title: Every question is asked three times
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the rule: each question is asked three times, and the crowd answers 'yes, yes, yes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked three times about each and every item, and they answered him: 'Yes, yes, yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the pattern: every question is asked three times. This sets up the question that comes next: why so much?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text printed only two rounds per question, but this line tells us that the real practice was three rounds for each item. The repetition is meant to make the event very public and very clear.

keyTerms.meaning: Three times.
Each and every item (each question).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get thrown by the count. Above, each question appears only twice, but this line tells you that the actual practice was three times for each one.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים עַל כׇּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר,
phrases.english: Three times for each and every matter,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: הֵין, הֵין, הֵין.
phrases.english: and they say to him: Yes, yes, yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים עַל כׇּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the questions in steps 5 and 6 as a rule of three times each.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each question in the עומר ceremony is asked three times, with a threefold 'yes'.

steps.title: Why is all this needed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why the ceremony needs so much public repetition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה stops to ask why such a loud, repeated show is necessary. It is setting up its own answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reaping barley does not normally need a crowd confirming every detail three times. The question points out that something unusual is going on, and that it must have a purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need all this?', asking why something is so excessive.

phrases.english: Why do I need all this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the repetition described in steps 5 through 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of making the עומר reaping so public and repetitive.

steps.title: Because of the בייתוסים
steps.stepSummary: The ceremony is made so public to oppose the בייתוסים, who said the עומר is not reaped on the night after the first day of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the בייתוסים, who used to say: the עומר is not reaped on the night after the יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. The loud public show is a protest against the בייתוסים and their wrong view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בייתוסים denied that the עומר is reaped right after the first day of פסח. By having the whole crowd loudly approve every detail at that exact time, the חכמים showed publicly that this is the correct time. That is also why the questions about שבת matter: the reaping goes ahead at its set time even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A group that disagreed with the חכמים about the תורה שבעל פה.
The reaping of the barley for the עומר offering.
The night after the יום טוב, here the night after the first day of פסח.

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר ceremony was made loud and public on purpose. It showed everyone, against the בייתוסים, that the עומר is reaped on the night after the first day of פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: The date of the עומר decides when counting begins, and so when שבועות falls. This is the link to the ברייתא the גמרא brings next.

phrases.english: Because of the Boethusians,
who would say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין קְצִירַת הָעוֹמֶר בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: There is no reaping of the omer at the conclusion of the Festival day.
phrases.notes: 'The Festival day' is the first day of פסח. The בייתוסים held that the reaping happens only at the end of a שבת.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The public, repeated confirmations were meant to oppose the בייתוסים, who denied reaping the עומר on the night after the first day of פסח.

steps.title: Days in ניסן with no fasting or eulogizing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא listing days on which fasting is forbidden, and on some, eulogizing too. These include 1 to 8 ניסן, for the fixing of the תמיד, and from 8 ניסן until the end of פסח, for the restoring of שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: These are the days on which one may not fast, and on some of them one may not eulogize either. From the first of ניסן until the eighth, the תמיד was firmly set up, so one may not eulogize. From the eighth until the end of the holiday, the festival of שבועות was restored, so one may not eulogize.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins with a ברייתא about special days of celebration in ניסן. It sets up a discussion connected to the משנה's argument with the בייתוסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These days were made into minor holidays because of victories in setting the correct practice. One was the proper bringing of the תמיד. The other was the correct date of שבועות, which depends on when the עומר is reaped, the very issue in the משנה. Because they are days of celebration, fasting and eulogizing are not allowed on them.

keyTerms.meaning: To fast.
To eulogize, to say a הספד for someone who died.
'The תמיד was established', meaning the daily offering was set up properly.
'The festival of שבועות was restored' to its correct date.
The holiday, here פסח.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
These are the days on which one may not fast,
and on some of them one may not eulogize.

phrases.aramaic: מֵרֵישׁ יַרְחָא דְּנִיסָן עַד תְּמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: From the New Moon of Nisan until the eighth of it,
the daily offering was established, so one may not eulogize,
and from the eighth of it until the end of the Festival,
the festival of Shavuot was restored, so one may not eulogize.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִלֵּין יוֹמַיָּא דְּלָא לְהִתְעַנָּאָה בְּהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a ברייתא tied to the משנה's argument with the בייתוסים over the עומר and the date of שבועות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting and eulogizing are forbidden from 1 to 8 ניסן, for the fixing of the תמיד, and from 8 ניסן to the end of פסח, for the restoring of שבועות.

steps.title: Why 1 to 8 ניסן is a happy time: the תמיד was fixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא line again and explains it. The צדוקים had claimed that one person could privately donate the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the first of ניסן until the eighth, the proper way of bringing the daily offering was established, so no eulogies are allowed. This is because the צדוקים used to say that one person could donate and bring the תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats one line of the ברייתא and explains what happened on those days. The צדוקים held a mistaken view about who pays for the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said the תמיד was 'established.' Now we learn what the fight was about. The צדוקים held that a private person could pay for the daily offering, while the accepted tradition is that it must come from public funds.

keyTerms.meaning: Sadducees, a group that rejected the oral tradition of the חכמים
The daily offering, brought every morning and afternoon
A private individual donates
Was established, set in its proper way

phrases.english: From the start of the month of Nisan
and until the eighth of it
the daily offering was established,
so one may not eulogize –
for the Sadducees would say:
An individual may donate and bring the daily offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵרֵישׁ יַרְחָא דְּנִיסָן וְעַד תְּמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ אִיתּוֹקַם תְּמִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the first period of the ברייתא from step 10 and explains the background.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days 1 to 8 ניסן celebrate defeating the צדוקים' claim that an individual may donate the תמיד.

steps.title: What פסוק did the צדוקים use?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the צדוקים based their view on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the צדוקים' claim. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before showing the answer of the חכמים, the גמרא wants to see the צדוקים' own argument from the פסוק. This way, both sides are laid out clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: They expounded, learned out from a פסוק

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the צדוקים' view stated in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse the צדוקים used to claim an individual may bring the תמיד.

steps.title: The צדוקים' פסוק: 'תעשה' in the singular
steps.stepSummary: The צדוקים learned from a פסוק about the תמיד that speaks to one person: 'you (singular) shall offer.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer in the afternoon.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק the צדוקים used. Its wording 'תעשה' speaks to one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תעשה is in the singular. The צדוקים read this to mean that any single person may offer the תמיד, so it does not have to come from the community.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb
You (one person) shall offer
In the afternoon, literally 'between the evenings'

phrases.english: "The one lamb you shall offer in the morning,
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:4. The word תעשה speaks to one person, and that is their whole proof.

phrases.english: and the other lamb
you shall offer in the afternoon."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צדוקים learned from the singular תעשה in במדבר 28:4.

steps.title: How did the חכמים answer them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reply the חכמים gave to the צדוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how the חכמים answered the צדוקים. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we have the צדוקים' proof, we need the counter-proof. The answer will explain how the חכמים won, which is why these days became days of celebration.

keyTerms.meaning: They replied, answered back

phrases.english: What did they reply?
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the חכמים, answering the צדוקים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the rebuttal to the צדוקים' proof from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse the חכמים used to refute the צדוקים.

steps.title: The חכמים' פסוק: 'תשמרו' in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים quoted a פסוק in the plural, 'תשמרו', showing that all the תמיד offerings come from the public Temple fund.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My offering, My food for My fires, you (plural) shall observe.' This teaches that all of them come from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer of the חכמים. A plural word shows that the תמיד belongs to the whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Against the singular תעשה, the חכמים point to the plural תשמרו. So the תמיד is the whole nation's offering and must be bought with public money, the תרומת הלשכה. Winning this argument is what made 1 to 8 ניסן a time of celebration.

keyTerms.meaning: My offering, My food: how the פסוק describes the תמיד
You (plural) shall observe
The public fund of the Temple chamber, collected from everyone's half-shekel

steps.whatToRemember: The תמיד is a community offering paid from public funds. The חכמים proved it from the plural תשמרו, against the צדוקים' singular תעשה.

phrases.english: "My offering, My food for My fires,
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:2. The key word is the next one, תשמרו, which speaks to many people.

phrases.english: you shall observe,"
meaning that they all should come
from the collection of the Temple treasury chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and overturns the proof of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural תשמרו shows that the תמיד comes from public funds, not from a private donor.

steps.title: Why 8 ניסן to the end of פסח: the date of שבועות was restored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the second period of the ברייתא. The בייתוסים claimed that שבועות always falls right after שבת, on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the eighth of ניסן until the end of the festival, the proper date of שבועות was restored, so no eulogies are allowed. This is because the בייתוסים used to say that עצרת is always after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and explains its background. The בייתוסים had a mistaken view about when שבועות falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to step 9, where the בייתוסים denied that the עומר is cut on the night after the first day of פסח. They read 'the day after שבת' as a real שבת, so the count would always start on Sunday and שבועות would always land on Sunday. The ברייתא celebrates that the correct date was restored.

keyTerms.meaning: Boethusians, a group that denied the oral tradition
Another name for שבועות
Was restored, put back in place
The end of the festival (of פסח)

phrases.english: From the eighth of it,
and until the end of the festival,
the festival of Shavuot was restored,
so one may not eulogize,
for the Boethusians would say:
Shavuot is after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְּמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ וְעַד סוֹף מוֹעֲדָא אִיתּוֹתַב חַגָּא דְשָׁבוּעַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second period listed in the ברייתא of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days 8 ניסן to the end of פסח celebrate defeating the בייתוסים' claim that שבועות is always on Sunday.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי demands their source
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי confronts the בייתוסים, calls them fools, and asks where they got their idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי joined them and said: Fools, where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי challenges the בייתוסים to show a real source for their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not asking out of curiosity. He is attacking them and showing that their view has no real backing. The challenge sets up the weak answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Joined in, took them on
Fools
From where do you get this?

phrases.aramaic: נִיטְפַּל לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai joined them,
and said to them: Fools,
from where do you get this?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיטְפַּל לָהֶם רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאָמַר לָהֶם שׁוֹטִים מִנַּיִן לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the בייתוסים' view stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בייתוסים' claim that שבועות is always on Sunday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He demands a source, implying they have none.

steps.title: An old man's answer: משה wanted a two-day celebration
steps.stepSummary: Nobody could answer except one old man, who babbled that משה put שבועות on Sunday so the Jews could enjoy a two-day holiday together with שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No one answered him except one old man who was babbling at him. He said: משה רבינו loved the Jewish people. He knew that עצרת is only one day, so he set it right after שבת, so that the Jews could enjoy themselves for two days.
steps.whatsHappening: Only one person tries to answer רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He gives a reason based on feelings instead of a source from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old man does not bring any פסוק. He only offers a reason for why the date would be nice. The word מפטפט (babbling) already tells us the גמרא does not take him seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: Babbling, talking nonsense
He set it up, arranged it
Enjoying themselves

phrases.english: And there was not one man
who answered him,
except for one old man
who was babbling at him,
and he said: Moses our teacher
was a lover of the Jewish people,
and he knew that Shavuot is one day,
so he went and set it after Shabbat
so that the Jewish people would
enjoy themselves for two days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיָה אָדָם אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מְשִׁיבוֹ חוּץ מִזָּקֵן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A reason with no source: משה put שבועות on Sunday so Israel would have two days of joy.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A reason-based defense with no source: משה set שבועות after שבת out of love for Israel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בייתוסים' view that שבועות always falls on Sunday has no source
steps.terutzMaskana: The old man claims the Sunday date comes from משה's wish to give Israel two days of joy. Step 19 rejects this.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers with a verse about the eleven-day journey
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי quotes against the old man a פסוק saying the trip from חורב is only an eleven-day journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: He quoted this פסוק against him: 'It is eleven days from חורב by way of הר שעיר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rejects the old man's 'משה loved Israel' reasoning by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא only quotes the פסוק; its point is spelled out on the next amud. The trip from חורב takes eleven days, yet Israel was kept in the desert forty years. So 'משה loved Israel' cannot prove that he arranged things to be pleasant for them.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק, verse
Another name for הר סיני
הר שעיר, on the route toward ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: The no-eulogy days of 8 ניסן until the end of פסח celebrate defeating the בייתוסים, whose only defense of a Sunday שבועות was a weak 'feel-good' reason.

phrases.english: He recited this verse about him:
"It is eleven days from Horeb
by the way of Mount Seir."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the old man's answer from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The old man's reasoning that משה changed the date out of love for Israel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'love of Israel' reasoning does not hold up, as the פסוק about the eleven-day journey hints.
